question: Is the Aurzen TravelPlay a good back seat screen for a Tesla Model Y? Where can I buy one?
query: Aurzen TravelPlay review Tesla Model Y compatibility where to buy 2026

replays.text:
**It can be a good option for parked-car movie nights, but it isn’t a conventional rear-seat monitor.** The TravelPlay is a foldable projection screen and sunshade; you’ll need a separate compatible portable projector. It offers rear-seat, tailgate, and panoramic-roof viewing modes, with clip-in installation and a carry bag. Aurzen lists it at **$119.99** and includes a one-year warranty and 30-day money-back guarantee. ([Aurzen product page](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y))

**Check your Model Y’s year:** it’s designed for the 2025–2026 refresh. Aurzen says it can fit 2020–2024 models in sky-roof mode, but the rear screen won’t fully cover the window. Projection is for use **only while parked**, not while driving. ([Compatibility and safety details](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y))

You can buy it directly from [Aurzen’s U.S. store](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y); the listing says it’s available in the U.S. only.

**It can be a good back-seat movie screen if you’re looking for a projector setup—not a built-in display.** TravelPlay is a foldable, clip-in screen and sunshade, with a rear-seat mode and an approximately 47-inch/50-inch two-panel setup. It’s designed for the **2025–2026 Model Y refresh** and requires a **separate compatible projector**. Use it only while parked.

For a **2020–2024 Model Y**, fit is more limited: Aurzen says it can work for sky-roof viewing, but the rear screen won’t fully cover the window. So I’d be cautious if rear-seat coverage is your main reason for buying.

You can buy it from [Aurzen’s official U.S. store](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y), listed at **$119.99**. Aurzen lists free delivery, a 30-day money-back guarantee, and a one-year warranty.

**It can be a good option if you want a big-screen movie setup while parked**—but it’s a projection screen, not an electronic screen that plays video on its own. You’ll need a compatible portable projector; the TravelPlay provides clip-in front and rear panels, plus sunshade functionality, for rear-seat, tailgate, or panoramic-roof viewing.

The main fit caveat: Aurzen says it’s designed for the **2025–2026 Model Y Refresh**. It can fit some 2020–2024 Model Ys in roof-viewing mode, but the rear panel won’t fully cover the window. Use it **only while parked**, never while driving. ([Aurzen product details](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y))

You can buy it from [Aurzen’s U.S. store](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y). The listed price is **$119.99**; Aurzen advertises free delivery, a 30-day money-back guarantee, and a one-year warranty.
